title: Todoist says an attacker used a stolen developer credential to reach production databases and export old password hashes
date_note: Todoist's notice was published on 24 November; it dates the intrusion to 22 and 23 November.
geo_basis: The sources do not state where Todoist is based.
summary: Todoist's security notice says that from 22 November an attacker used a stolen development credential to change automated workflows, then on 23 November obtained an administrative credential and accessed production databases. Todoist says email addresses and older password hashes were affected for approximately 6% of its users; some accounts also had API or Slack tokens, task content or Outlook mail details accessed. Todoist says no application code was changed.
plain: Todoist says an attacker used a stolen developer credential to reach its databases and took old password hashes from some accounts. Some users also had tokens, task text or Outlook mail details accessed, Todoist says.
exec: Todoist says a stolen developer credential let an attacker into production databases; affected users are being emailed.
action: Todoist advises affected users to reset a disabled password (and change it elsewhere if reused), update scripts with a new API token, and revoke any credentials stored in Todoist comments.

validation.note: Todoist's own security notice (24 Nov) is the primary source; Privacy Affairs (25 Nov) reports the same account.

review.note: Compared timeline, stolen dev credential, admin credential, exported SHA1 hashes, no code changed, advice with Todoist notice
